services.name: Balloon History
services.desc: Ballooning History During the 13th century Roger Bacon, the great English friar and philosopher, wrote that man could fly if he was fastened to a large hollow ball of thin copper, filled with liquid fire or air. As centuries passed other dreamers postulate similar ideas, but it remained for the Montgolfier brothers of France to reduce the dreams to reality. They learned how to put a pan of burning charcoal beneath a hole in a large cloth bag. In September of 1783, with King Louis XVI watching, they put a duck, a rooster and a sheep in a basket slung beneath their cloth balloon.
